description: CexChain protocol objects of specification revision v0.14 (claims), built by an independent Python encoder from spec/README.md and spec/cexchain.cddl. `claim_type` is the fifth mechanism type's lifecycle (initial state "confirmed", no transitions, no roles; withdrawn by revoking it). `claim_metadata` holds claim metadata (record key 5) on its own: `valid` cases, each its deterministic CBOR (`metadata`), its condition as JSON, and the condition in words (`text`, section 11, "A claim in words"), the specification's own example first; `refused` cases, each breaking one rule of the `claim` CDDL or its limits in section 6, which `why` names: "unknown key", "missing key", "source" (not a 32-byte id), "condition" (not 1 to 16 terms), "term" (not [field, op, type, value]), "field" (not 1 to 64 bytes of text), "operator", "type", "operator and type" (an order operator on text, exists on another type), "value" (not the shape the operator takes: one value, [low, high], 1 to 64 values, or null for exists), "number", "money", "date", "text" (a value that is not one of the type), "order" (between with low above high), "distinct" (in with a value twice), "holds", "as_of", "until" (not after as_of), "subject", "for". `ledgers` holds an employer's ledger for each hash: the organization delegates employment records (example.org.employment/1) and claims to a clerk, who registers records and claims on them. Each statement registers at its `registered_at` (the log entries carry it). `refused` statements are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at `at`, and break exactly one rule, which `why` names: "role" and "transition" (a claim takes neither), "no such source", "source of a mechanism type" (here another claim), "source revoked", "source superseded", "as_of after registration", "mechanism" (a claim neither supersedes nor is superseded), "revoked" (a revoked claim takes nothing more), "no metadata", and the metadata rules above ("unknown key", "operator and type"); every refused statement parses, since a claim's metadata is checked by the ledger rules. A claim's registration is a statement about the claim only: its source's history does not list it. `claims` lists the accepted claims, and `records` gives each record's type, state, revocation, registrant, history, versions, and, for a claim, what a report states of it (section 11) at the checkpoint: its source, the source's type and status ("live", "revoked", or "replaced" by a newer version), the condition and its words, holds, as_of and until (ms), whether `checkpoint_time` is past until (`lapsed`), the subject, and the access request it answers (`for`). `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` (signed at `checkpoint_time`) covers it. Signatures are Ed25519 (deterministic); keys are throwaway: seed = SHA-256("CexChain test key: <name>").

statements.name: genesis
register the clerk
delegate employment records and claims to the clerk
register an employment record
the clerk claims the specification's example of it
the organization claims a condition that does not hold
register a second employee's record
a new version supersedes it
a claim on the new version, until two minutes later
register a third employee's record
the organization revokes it
the organization's version supersedes the second record's
the clerk withdraws the first claim by revoking it
the organization revokes the first record
a claim on the latest version

refused.name: a claim on a record that does not exist
a claim on a mechanism record, the first claim
a claim evaluated after its registration
a claim whose metadata has an unknown key
a claim whose condition is malformed (exists on a number)
a claim that supersedes a record
a record that supersedes the claim
a claim on the superseded version
a claim on the revoked record
a claim on the first record, revoked since
